b: Information especially in the healthcare field has been democratized with the Internet and most importantly with AI. Many doctors do not have the patients’ best interests in mind, they have to balance their business needs along with patient needs, and many times the money can come first. This mostly applies to outpatient centers where the staff needs enough volume and billing to turn a profit. I’ve seen so many examples of people in healthcare complaining about patients “doing their own research” and arguing with them during their appointment. As individuals we have a responsibility to ourselves and need to do our own due diligence and gather multiple opinions before making a decision. I understand that complex surgical procedures and long medication schedules are best handled by experts because the average person can’t realistically figure this out on their own. But for the remaining “routine” issues it’s perfectly reasonable for people to do their own research, consult AI tools that are arguably more effective than doctors in some cases and then have a discussion with their doctors to figure out the best treatment plan for them that balances cost and effectiveness.
